newsitem.title: USA: NYPA sees Indian Point 3 nuke on line late Thurs.
newsitem.headline: NYPA sees Indian Point 3 nuke on line late Thurs.

text.p: New York Power Authority's (NYPA) 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 3 nuclear power station was expected to return on line late Thursday after its output was cut Wednesday for electrical work, the utility said.
"Work's completed. We're on our way back," a spokesman for the state power agency said.
Technicians needed to reposition an electrical conduit in the part of the wiring for the system that monitors the flow of electricity from Indian Point 3's generator.
Electricity production from the plant in Buchanan, N.Y., bottomed at five percent of capacity, the spokesman said.

The 800 MW Fitzpatrick station in Scriba, N.Y., NYPA's other nuclear plant, continued to operate at 70 percent power amid repairs to one of its feedwater pump, according to Nuclear Regulatory Commission's daily status report on Thursday.
NYPA produces about a fourth of all electricity generated in the state of New York.
